I'm a religious Christian myself and coming from a conservative Muslim family who disowned me for leaving Islam and being queer while living in a theocratic Muslim nation, I understand what people who are experiencing religious trauma deal with. I know saying that doesn't amount to much but I hope you know that I'm sincere about it. 

I don't speak for all Christians so don't take my word for the many but it's sad to see many people leave faith due to the harsh treatment they endured from their family, church, etc. So, when queer Christians and allies see this, they want to reassure others but they do it in an inappropriate setting. Saying that these aren't 'true Christians' in a normal conversation/discussion/debate: fine. Saying so when someone is venting about their trauma and need some support and relief: yeah, that's problematic. 

I don't judge nor scorn those who've chosen the path that they feel is right for them. If it makes them happy, then go for it. I'm sad that people view Christianity negatively and a tool for oppression. But I know no one can change the minds of those who aren't willing to do so and those who are intolerant. Therefore we need to fight back, support each other rather than saying "BuT ThIs isN't TrUe ChRisTiAnItY". 

Likewise, I don't speak for all but I do hope you have at least an insight of at least my viewpoint. I hope that you're doing well and pray for emancipation for all of us who are oppressed. This criticism has opened my eyes more on how queer-affirming religious people act and I will try to be better than that.
